extras.name: New York City
extras.note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid, the 1865 shoreline, the squares and church footprints carry the fit; the 1811 and 1865 sheets span the island beyond the 2000 m town box, so those fits are likely to end review items (the Venice precedent, docs/lead_artists.md)

extras.name: Washington, D.C.
extras.note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid, the diagonal avenues, the Potomac shoreline and the squares carry the fit; the 1865 defences ring spans ~35 km beyond the 2000 m town box, so that fit is likely to end a review item (the Venice precedent, docs/lead_artists.md); the ring's forts are candidate kind-'fort' sites and the catalog already has the individuals (Fort Bayard Q3077774, Fort DeRussy Q5471024, Fort Totten Q18150335, Fort Marcy Q61784495, Fort Foote Q14691922, all part_of Q5124610 'Civil War defenses of Washington, D.C.' - data/catalog/sites.jsonl)

extras.name: San Francisco
extras.note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid, the bay shoreline (the 1854 sheet's red water-front line), the squares and the hills carry the fit; the 1849/1850 sheets draw the old peninsula tip to tip in the 2000 m town box (~30 m overshoot at each drawn tip); the point is the midpoint of the two drawn tips (Washington & Jones / Rincon Point), not a P625 (see the SITES comment); the 1854 sheet's 1850s growth (the Center Street grid, the Market & 10th-11th corner) reaches past the box's SW corner - likely a review item (the NY 1811 precedent, docs/lead_artists.md)

extras.name: Nashville
extras.note: aerial-photograph ground (no open LiDAR over the built-up city: bare-earth LiDAR erases the streets); the street grid, the Cumberland shoreline, the squares and the church footprints carry the fit; the point is the center of the projected 1804 drawn extent (the 147/148 SF precedent) - P625 is 721 m NE and its 2000 m box overshoots the drawn extent W 543 m, so it is not a P625; the 1804 Clayton plan is a near north-up bird's-eye view (~6 deg tilt, 0.852 m/px); the other three staged sheets span beyond the 2000 m town box, so their fits are likely to end review items (the NY 1811 / DC 1865 ring precedent); Fort Negley Q5471744 (drawn on the 1895 plate) gets a fort site of its own (1600 m box, a 3DEP LiDAR candidate) only when a fort-only plan is found - none is on Commons (the 3 Fletcher 1864 views are 236b leads)

files.desc: New York City on the eve of Revolution. The only privately held copy in full contemporary color of the "finest map of an American city and its environs produced in the eighteenth century" (Cohen & Augustyn, Manhattan in Maps). The map itself is a highly accurate delineation of the bustling seaport of some twenty thousand people as it existed in the late 1760s at the southern tip of Manhattan Island. files.desc: Plan of Yerba Buena (which was later renamed to San Francisco), as laid out by Jean Jacques Vioget. The map itself dates to 1839, but was published in 1853 as part of a deposition; oriented with north to the right and centered on  Portsmouth Square ; bounded on the right (north) by Pacific, on the left (south) by Washington), on the top (west) by Grant, and on the bottom (east) by Montgomery.
